planting.note: Set divisions or container plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; this patented sport was selected from a Japanese breeding program for richer, darker foliage color than standard Japanese spurge.

directions: Hakurei arose as a naturally occurring branch sport of common Japanese spurge selected in Utsunomiya, Japan, and is grown for its glossy, deep dark-green whorled foliage that reads noticeably richer than the species. Plant divisions in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in dense shade under trees, where it forms the same tidy, slow-spreading evergreen carpet as typical Pachysandra terminalis. Small white flower spikes appear in early spring but are secondary to the foliage display.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; this rare selection, introduced by Don Jacobs of Eco Gardens, is grown chiefly for exceptionally heavy silver mottling on the blue-green leaves.

directions: Eco Treasure Island is an uncommon Allegheny spurge selection valued for its heavily silver-mottled, blue-green leaves, which intensify in pattern through the growing season and into fall. Plant in deep, dry shade under deciduous trees where it slowly spreads by rhizomes to form a textured native groundcover, and leave the previous year's mottled foliage in place through winter since it persists semi-evergreen and still provides cover when the fragrant, pale pink late-winter flower spikes emerge at the base of the clumps.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or divisions in spring or fall in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in partial to full shade; Sterling Silver is grown for its cream-and-green variegated foliage rather than speed of coverage.

directions: Sterling Silver carries glossy leaves splashed with green, gray-green, and creamy white, giving it a brighter presence in deep shade than solid-green periwinkle cultivars. Clear blue, five-petaled flowers appear in spring against the variegated mat, which spreads gradually by rooting stems to form a dense, weed-suppressing evergreen carpet under trees and on shaded slopes.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or divisions in spring or fall in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in partial to full shade; this variegated cultivar grows more slowly than green-leaved periwinkle, so space plantings closer for quicker cover.

directions: Blue and Gold pairs green-and-gold variegated foliage with the typical lavender-blue, pinwheel-shaped spring flowers of lesser periwinkle, lighting up dense shade under trees where solid-green groundcovers read flat. It spreads slowly by rooting stems into a low, dense evergreen mat; shear lightly in late winter to remove tattered foliage and keep the variegation fresh for the new season.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or divisions in spring or fall in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in partial shade to full shade; this patented sport arose as a branch mutation on standard periwinkle and is somewhat less vigorous than the green-leaved species.

directions: New growth on 24 Carat emerges bright gold before gradually fading to green, giving the low evergreen mat seasonal two-tone interest beneath its light blue spring flowers. It is slightly less vigorous than ordinary periwinkle, so site it in a spot with some bright, filtered light under high tree canopy rather than deep, dense shade to keep the gold color strongest.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or divisions in spring or fall in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in partial to full shade; Emily Joy is grown for its unusually large, abundant white flowers rather than foliage color.

directions: Emily Joy is a free-flowering, white-blossomed periwinkle noted for larger, more generously produced blooms than the common white form, carried over glossy dark green foliage from early spring into summer. It spreads at a restrained, manageable pace by rooting stems, forming a dense evergreen mat well suited to shaded beds under trees and foundation plantings where brightness in deep shade is wanted without aggressive spread.
